_README: STAGE THREE — the wants expressed in Ordo.
Each entry was written FROM THE WANT, not translated from the stage-two
SQL: the point is whether the language can say the intent, not whether it
can transliterate a SELECT. The compiler and the seeded database decide
which of four verdicts each attempt earns:
equivalent            compiles, and returns exactly the want's rows
compile_error         the compiler refused it — my Ordo is wrong, or
the compiler has a gap; the runner fails loudly
semantic_divergence   compiles and returns DIFFERENT rows — the most
serious class, and the runner fails on it
inexpressible         no Ordo spelling exists for the intent; recorded
with the reason, because these feed the spec
An entry is either {"ordo": "..."} — which the runner requires to be
equivalent — or {"inexpressible": "reason"}. If a claimed inexpressible
later compiles, the runner fails: progress must force reclassification,

W014.ordo:
people[org, salary]
group org { total: sum salary }

W015.ordo:
people[org, age]
group org { people: count, withAge: sum cond(age is null -> 0, 1) }
W015.note: Ordo's count takes no argument — counting the non-null values of a column has no direct spelling and needs the sum-of-cond workaround. Expressible, but the ergonomic gap is real and is exactly what judged wants exist to weigh.

W026.ordo:
taskTags[title: task.title]
group title { tags: count }

W039.note: Reclassified 2026-08-12: ruling 1's spelling now compiles and runs — distinct settles the rows, reduce counts them. Was inexpressible while reduce did not exist.

W049.inexpressible: The want demands the mean as an INTEGER, computed as sum of non-null over count of non-null. Ordo has `avg`, but avg's result type is a decimal, and the grammar has no arithmetic OVER aggregates — `sum age / count` is not a spelling. So the integer mean is unreachable: avg gives 36.0000000000000000-shaped output and nothing can divide two aggregates. A language question the spec owes an answer: what is the declared result type of avg over int, and is aggregate arithmetic ever legal?
W049.ruling: Ruled 2026-08-11: avg returns exact decimal; there is no arithmetic over aggregates. The integer mean is inexpressible BY DESIGN, not by gap — this entry stays in the pinned set permanently.

W050.ordo:
teams[team: name]  people[]
group team { n: count }
W050.note: Reclassified 2026-08-12: ruling 3's settled multi-source spelling compiles and runs — teams anchor, people joined outer-preserving on the inferred people.team edge, bare count masked to the many side so Platform counts 0. Was inexpressible while multi-source did not exist.

W052.ordo:
tasks[points, org: project.org.name]
group org { points: sum points }

W055.note: The want asks for the raise in exact integer minor units. `/` yields decimal at a fixed fractional scale of 12 (definition-language.md §2, Division), so the bare `salary * 105 / 100` is a decimal and does not land in an integer projection on its own — `round(x, 0)` is where the attempt states its boundary. The earlier spelling read as integer arithmetic and was lowered to `bigint / bigint`, which truncates; it happened to agree here only because every salary in the fixture divides exactly.

W058.ordo: people(age > 40 or lastSeen is not null)[name]
